thread:
sara: quick upload of last night's sparse-tiling + dim/batch sweep across eu-west and us-west. tl;dr: tiling helps CPU for high dims, GPU wins for small dims but PCIe in apac will matter.

liam: nice — can you drop the perf table or a short summary?

sara: pasted summary below (p95 lat in ms, throughput qps where relevant):
```
model: reranker-v2-small-sparse
vec_dims: [64, 128, 256, 512]
batch: [1,8,32,128]
configs: cpu-tiling-int8, cpu-no-tiling-int8, gpu-cutlass-fp16, gpu-triton-int8
regions: eu-west, us-west, apac-south (proxying via us-west)
```
results (selected):
- 64d x b1: gpu-cutlass 18ms p95 / 55 qps, cpu-tiling 80ms p95 / 12 qps
- 128d x b8: gpu-triton-int8 22ms p95 / 210 qps, cpu-tiling 95ms p95 / 75 qps (vectorized)
- 256d x b32: gpu-cutlass 40ms p95 / 520 qps, cpu-tiling 210ms p95 / 220 qps
- 512d x b128: gpu-triton 160ms p95 / 720 qps, cpu-tiling 700ms p95 / 420 qps

note: cpu-no-tiling was ~2-3x slower at >=256 dims due to cache misses; tiling brought it down 30-50% and improved L1/L2 locality.

ana: interesting — what quantization path did you use on CPU? 8-bit symmetric or per-channel?

sara: per-channel asymmetric int8 for CPU, small outlier corrections applied. GPU FP16 for cutlass; triton used int8 kernels with channel scales.

jon: how bad was apac proxying? any PCIe saturations or extra tail?

sara: apac-south (we proxied requests through us-west because private infra wasn't in region) showed +25-40ms added network p95 and occasional p99 spikes when we saturated 1GbE egress on the test VM. raw kernel times were same but end-to-end latency suffered.

liam: did you test NVLink vs PCIe cases for multi-GPU batching?

sara: single-GPU benchmarks only. Multi-GPU tiling/concat overheads look small in synthetic tests but need a real cluster run. filing an infra ticket to schedule dedicated multi-gpu slot.

perf-bot: automated-check: all runs used the standardized harness v3.4, seed=42, 10 warmup iterations, 200 measured iterations. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/reranker/sparse-tiling/1977654321.tar.gz

liam: can you attach the kernel profiler snippets? curious about GEMM vs gather costs for sparse vectors.

sara: attaching small snippet from perf trace (excerpt):
```
# gpu-cutlass: GEMM 65%, kernel-launch 8%, memcopy 12%
# cpu-tiling-int8: gather 40%, matmul 35%, cache-evict 12%, other 13%
```

ana: that gather number on CPU is a red flag — might be worth prepacking indices or reordering dims to improve stride locality. also consider AVX512 tiling for eu-west nodes that have it.

sara: agreed. next steps: 1) try prepacked index layout + run 128/256 dims again on cpu-tiling, 2) schedule a multi-gpu NVLink run, 3) re-run apac in-region once infra is available (to remove proxy noise).

jon: any customer-impacting recommendations?

sara: for now recommend: default to gpu-triton-int8 for small dims and high-qps endpoints; enable cpu-tiling-int8 fallback for mid dims where GPUs are constrained. add region-aware routing to prefer in-region GPUs to avoid proxy tails.

liam: SGTM. can you drop the full CSV into the bench dashboard and tag me? I'll slice by instance type and kernel.

sara: done, CSV uploaded and dashboard updated. tag: @liam. linking artifacts and run config in the ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-821

ana: nice work, small follow-up — can you capture the eval delta for reranker quality when switching to int8? even small precision regressions matter.

sara: already ran holdout eval: MRR delta vs fp16: -0.9% on dev-cluster, worst case -1.6% on short queries. logging full eval in the artifacts.

perf-bot: note: there is an open quantization-regressions alert for reranker-v2-small, severity: low, owner: ana.

liam: cool. let's sync after the prepack runs. thanks all :thumbsup:
